findings.location: ## Definition, Fourier coefficients: the L1 real-valuedness equivalence
findings.evidence: The reverse implication relies on L1 Fourier uniqueness and cites thm-fejer-convergence-in-lp, but that supplier is absent from this item's deps. The included Fourier-basis theorem is stated for L2 and does not supply general L1 uniqueness.

findings.location: ## Definition, operators: “a scalar field f ... in the analogous scalar spaces”
findings.evidence: The item defines H^s(T^3;R^3), but only names “analogous scalar spaces” without defining their coefficient families, norms, or scalar H^s notation. The pressure item then asserts p belongs to H^m as a scalar field.

findings.location: ## Statement, claims 2–3; ## Proof, steps 4.1 and 5.1
findings.evidence: The integral is introduced only for a<b, but G(a)=integral_a^a g is required, claim 3 allows c=a or c=b, and step 4.1 uses zero-length subintegrals. Step 5.1 also invokes the same argument for negative increments without an oriented-integral convention. Define these cases or rewrite the uses.

findings.location: ## Proof, step 3.1
findings.evidence: The displayed comparison ends with a right-hand expression containing an unbound m and the word “summed”; it is not a well-formed inequality. The subsequent “more explicitly” sentence gives the intended finite-partial-sum estimate, but the preceding computation should be replaced.

findings.location: ## Facts & Assumptions, F1
findings.evidence: The asserted multi-index weighted l1 estimate is justified only by (2π|k|∞)^|α|≤w_k^|α|≤w_k^(2σ'). A pointwise bound by w_k^(2σ') does not establish summability. The cited lattice lemma's general weight-sum claim plus weighted Cauchy–Schwarz supplies the estimate, but that argument is absent.

findings.location: ## Proof, step 2.2
findings.evidence: The proof uses a metric ball B(x0,delta) in T^3, but the declared structure is the quotient/product topology and no metric on T^3 is defined by the item or its dependencies. Use an open neighborhood or specify a metric.

findings.location: ## Proof, step 3.1
findings.evidence: The termwise-differentiation argument invokes the fundamental theorem of calculus on a torus segment for each finite Fourier sum. No FTC supplier is in deps and no local derivation is given.

findings.location: ## Statement, claim 3
findings.evidence: The input u is an H^sigma equivalence class, while C^j is a class of pointwise fields. Claim 1 constructs the unique representative tilde u, but claim 3 says “u is in C^j”; state that the canonical representative tilde u has this regularity.

findings.location: ## Statement, claim 2 and Facts & Assumptions F5
findings.evidence: The item fixes H^sigma as vector fields into R^3, then writes fg and the coefficient product hat f(l) hat g(k-l) without defining a vector multiplication or output type. Specify scalar inputs or define the intended componentwise/tensor product.

findings.location: ## Facts & Assumptions, F6; ## Proof, step 2.1
findings.evidence: F6 uses u tensor u and div(u tensor u), but the dependencies define divergence only for vector fields and do not define a tensor product or matrix divergence. Define those operations or give the componentwise product-rule identity used to show the mean is zero.

findings.location: ## Proof, steps 1.1 and 4.1
findings.evidence: The proof establishes that X_N is spanned by finitely many vectors and then fixes an ordered basis, but cites no finite spanning-set-to-basis result and supplies no elimination argument.

findings.location: ## Facts & Assumptions, F2
findings.evidence: The cited product supplier gives H^sigma×H^sigma→H^sigma and H^sigma×H^(sigma+1)→H^sigma for sigma>3/2. It does not state the claimed transport map H^p×H^p→H^(p−1) for every p>3/2. The proof can use sufficiently high orders, but this broader fact needs proof or a narrower hypothesis.

findings.location: ## Proof, step 2.1
findings.evidence: An H^p-valued derivative u'=G does not identify the pointwise time derivative until evaluation at x is applied as a bounded linear functional. The embedding gives that bound, but the proof does not make this step when concluding joint C^1 regularity.

findings.location: ## Proof, step 3.1
findings.evidence: The integral identity is asserted for t in [0,T], including t=0, but the cited Riemann-curve integral supplier only defines the integral for positive interval length and does not define integral_0^0. Handle t=0 separately or state the convention.

findings.location: ## Proof, step 4.1
findings.evidence: The equation has been established for Sobolev orders m>=s, but this paragraph says to take an integer m>=p for arbitrary p. Choose m>=max(s,p); the stated choice alone does not ensure the proved equation is available.

findings.location: ## Statement, claim 1
findings.evidence: p is a real scalar field, but H^m in the cited definition is defined for R^3-valued fields; the supplier only mentions undefined “analogous scalar spaces.” State or define scalar Sobolev spaces before asserting p belongs to H^m.

findings.location: ## Facts & Assumptions, F3
findings.evidence: The product estimate supplied by lem-discrete-young-and-sobolev-product requires m>3/2, but F3 states it without that restriction. The proof later uses bounds at r>3/2, so the fact should state its scope.

findings.location: ## Proof, step 3.1
findings.evidence: Equal Fourier coefficients imply q−p=0 almost everywhere by Fourier coefficient injectivity/Parseval, but the cited embedding claim 2 only says continuous fields equal almost everywhere are equal everywhere. The proof omits the coefficient-injectivity step needed before applying that claim.

findings.location: Page summary, paragraph beginning “The nonlinear core”
findings.evidence: The summary says the pressure-reconstruction item is “line 12.” In the page's ordered item list, thm-local-smooth-periodic-euler-viscous-solution is item 12 and lem-periodic-pressure-reconstruction is item 13.
